title: Jupiter: The Giant Planet That's a Failed Star
summary:
Imagine a planet so big that 1,300 Earths could fit inside it. That's Jupiter, the king of our solar system! It's not like Earth at all—it's a giant ball of gas, mostly hydrogen and helium. If you tried to stand on it, you'd just sink down into clouds of ammonia and water vapor, and the pressure would crush you. Not a fun vacation spot!

But from a spaceship, Jupiter looks amazing. Its clouds whip around at more than 300 miles per hour, making colorful stripes and swirls. The Great Red Spot is a giant hurricane that has been raging for hundreds of years. It's so big that nearly three Earths could fit across it!

Jupiter has almost 70 moons. One of them, Ganymede, is bigger than the planet Mercury and has its own magnetic field. Another moon, Io, is covered in volcanoes that shoot yellow sulfur 300 miles high—that's like stacking 50 Mount Everests! And Europa, an icy moon, might have a liquid ocean hiding under its frozen crust. Scientists think there could even be life in that ocean!

But watch out: Jupiter gives off crazy radiation, more than a thousand times the amount that would kill a person. So if you ever visit, keep your shields up. And here's a fun fact: even though Jupiter is the biggest planet, it has the shortest day—just 10 hours! That's because it spins super fast. So if you lived there (you can't, but just imagine), you'd have a really short school day.
why_it_matters: Studying Jupiter helps you see how different other planets can be from Earth, and why scientists look at moons like Europa for clues about life beyond our home.

background_read: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system and is named after the Roman king of the gods.
Planets made mostly of hydrogen and helium are called gas giants; Jupiter is the biggest gas giant of all.
Spacecraft have visited Jupiter to study its clouds, moons, and powerful magnetic field.

perspectives.description: They see Jupiter as an amazing 'king' planet with colorful clouds, huge storms, and many moons to study.
They warn that Jupiter's radiation and crushing pressure make it far too dangerous for people to visit.
They are especially excited about Europa, an icy moon that might hide a liquid ocean and maybe even life.
